items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: There was another fellow by the name of Don Chase. Don Chase played piano at the same time as Vic did at the Sanga.

ctx.x: Well, he played at the Little Club. He had a band up there. I don't know if he had Tony Papalia playing up there with him. I just don't remember the exact combination that he had up there. And then he played at the Sanga. That was one of the feature spots that he played in the days when the Sanga had stage shows. He was a great standby there. In fact, he did lots of solos on the stage. They let him do lots of solos. Yeah, he was one of the real fine piano players around here. Another fine piano player was Howard…
Were these guys jazz musicians? Captain Chase?

Well, I guess they probably played with dance bands. Let's put it this way, that they played with dance bands. I wouldn't know what he would exactly call them real jazz musicians because as I said, they were more or less legitimate. Readers. But I guess they did play with dance bands. There was another fellow by the name of Wilson that used to play piano. I think he played at the Lowest State. I can't think of his first name now. But he was quite an accomplished musician himself.
